headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: OpenHands can write/egress broadly while the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and undocumented for pairwise interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between data-engineering-zoomcamp and OpenHands, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or files in OpenHands' runtime, which is an unusual configuration for this pair. Because uncertainty must escalate, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies OpenHands output into course materials or prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared mounted workspace is added between the two, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Do not copy raw model output into the other agent's prompt.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared MCP bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: data-engineering-zoomcamp touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces, while OpenHands reads and writes only files mounted into its runtime. With no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, leakage is limited and not default. The pairwise pathway is therefore low, not medium.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into OpenHands' runtime, those files can be exposed in its outputs.
IF the course repo is mounted alongside private data, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Mount only the minimum necessary files.
Keep secrets out of the runtime volume.
Use separate mounts for public course content and private data.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and does not constrain shared state. If both are pointed at the same repo or mounted volume, OpenHands can overwrite or commit changes without coordination. The interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable directory, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF OpenHands is allowed to commit to a shared repo, it can race with other editors.
mitigations: Disable git write access for OpenHands when not needed.
Add a manual review step before commits.
Lock the repository during automated edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files and git state, so if it consumes outputs derived from data-engineering-zoomcamp without verification, mistakes can cascade into edits or commits. The zoomcamp profile itself is not an active agent, so the pathway is indirect and not default, but the downstream action authority in OpenHands makes medium appropriate.
conditions: IF OpenHands is instructed to treat generated text from the course repo as authoritative, it may propagate errors.
IF OpenHands is allowed to commit or execute changes based on unverified summaries, cascades can occur.
mitigations: Ask OpenHands to cite source files for claims.
Use a verification prompt before any action-taking step.
Restrict OpenHands to read-only mode for analysis tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data class mismatch is documented for data-engineering-zoomcamp, and OpenHands only lists model-provider API keys plus mounted files. With no PHI, EU PII, or policy mismatch evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established for this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into OpenHands, compliance analysis must be revisited.
IF the operator routes EU PII or PHI through either agent, new obligations may apply.
mitigations: Keep API keys in the provider's secret store.
